aspect.definition: Attack with maximum efficiency and dish out lots of damage. This aspect is a great fit for players who prefer fast-paced, fiery playstyles that break through opponents’ defenses and hurl themselves toward victory at any cost. A leader or base provides aspects; a card in another aspect costs 2 extra resources per icon the leader and base do not provide (aspect penalty).
aspect.strategicValue: Chosen for fast decks that win by dealing damage quickly; it pairs with cheap, aggressive units.

aspect.definition: Accelerate your resources and call upon lots of units or strengthen the units you already have in play. This is the aspect of choice for players who want to overwhelm their opponents with a massive board presence. A leader or base provides aspects; a card in another aspect costs 2 extra resources per icon the leader and base do not provide (aspect penalty).
aspect.strategicValue: Chosen for decks that ramp resources and flood the board; it rewards a wide board of units.

aspect.definition: Adapt to any situation on the fly with powerful, immediate effects and lots of tools for disrupting your opponent’s plans. This aspect is a perfect fit for players who prefer to respond quickly to threats and have an answer for anything their opponent could throw their way. A leader or base provides aspects; a card in another aspect costs 2 extra resources per icon the leader and base do not provide (aspect penalty).
aspect.strategicValue: Chosen for decks that answer threats and disrupt the opponent with flexible, immediate effects.

aspect.definition: Fight for peace and justice with cards that feature the protagonists of the Star Wars series. This aspect is great for players who want their cards to support and protect each other while pressing the attack. A leader or base provides aspects; a card in another aspect costs 2 extra resources per icon the leader and base do not provide (aspect penalty).
aspect.strategicValue: Chosen for decks built around heroic characters that protect each other; usually paired with a second aspect.

aspect.definition: Play defensively with the ability to heal damage, remove dangerous units from play, and protect your base from enemy attacks. This aspect is perfect for players who like patient playstyles that can endure even the deadliest assaults. A leader or base provides aspects; a card in another aspect costs 2 extra resources per icon the leader and base do not provide (aspect penalty).
aspect.strategicValue: Chosen for defensive decks that heal, remove threats and protect the base.

aspect.definition: Battle for ultimate power with cards that feature the antagonists of the Star Wars series. This aspect is perfect for players who want to command huge armies or wield powerful destructive effects. A leader or base provides aspects; a card in another aspect costs 2 extra resources per icon the leader and base do not provide (aspect penalty).
aspect.strategicValue: Chosen for decks built around villainous characters and big destructive effects; usually paired with a second aspect.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Ambush (After you play this unit, he may ready and attack an enemy unit.)
keyword.strategicValue: Lets a unit attack the turn it is played, so it removes a blocker or finishes a damaged unit immediately.

keyword.definition: Bounty is a keyword followed by a dash and ability text, and the text is different on each card. It resolves like a "When Defeated/When Captured" ability that an opponent controls and may choose to collect; collecting it is optional. Example reminder text on one card: Bounty — Draw a card. (When this unit is defeated or captured, your opponent collects its bounty.) Across all sets and printings, 138 printings of 33 distinct cards (counted by title and subtitle) carry it. Among the 1609 in-scope cards, 0 carry it.
keyword.strategicValue: A drawback on the unit that carries it: the opponent who defeats or captures the unit may collect the reward.

keyword.definition: Coordinate is a keyword followed by a dash and ability text, and the text is different on each card. It works like the constant ability "While you control 3 or more units, this card gains the following ability"; each Coordinate ability is independent, and a unit keeps the keyword while the ability after the dash is inactive. Example reminder text on one card: Coordinate — Action [Exhaust]: Attack with a unit. It gets +1/+0 for this attack. (Gain this ability while you control 3 or more units.) Across all sets and printings, 89 printings of 23 distinct cards (counted by title and subtitle) carry it. Among the 1609 in-scope cards, 0 carry it.
keyword.strategicValue: Rewards a wide board: the bonus switches on once you control three or more units.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Exploit 2 (While playing this card, defeat up to 2 units you control. This card costs 2 resources less for each unit defeated this way.)
keyword.strategicValue: Trades board presence for a cheaper big unit; strong when you hold cheap units you are happy to lose.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Fortify (Attach this to your base, not a unit.)
keyword.strategicValue: Puts an upgrade on your base instead of a unit, so it cannot be lost when a unit is defeated or bounced. What it then does varies widely: some give every friendly unit Overwhelm, Raid or +1/+0, some draw cards or deal damage to units, some exhaust or stall enemy units, and only a few protect or heal the base.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Grit (This unit gets +1/+0 for each damage on it.)
keyword.strategicValue: Makes a damaged unit hit harder, so it is better after it has taken a hit.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Hidden (This unit can't be attacked if it was played this phase.)
keyword.strategicValue: Protects a freshly played unit from attacks for one phase, giving it safe tempo.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Overwhelm (When attacking an enemy unit, deal excess damage to the opponent's base.)
keyword.strategicValue: Turns spare damage into base damage when attacking units, which speeds the race.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Piloting [3 resources Vigilance Villainy] (You may play this as an upgrade on a friendly Vehicle without a Pilot.)
keyword.strategicValue: Lets a unit be played as an upgrade on a Vehicle, giving flexibility between a body and a boost.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Plot (When you deploy a leader, you may play this card from your resources, paying its cost. Replace it with the top card of your deck.)
keyword.strategicValue: Lets a card be played from your resources when you deploy a leader, so deploying also gains card advantage.
keyword.source: card text (reminder text on the cards); the rules digest predates it

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Raid 2 (This unit gets +2/+0 while attacking.)
keyword.strategicValue: Adds power only on offence, so it favours decks that attack first.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Restore 1 (When this unit attacks, heal 1 damage from your base.)
keyword.strategicValue: Heals your base each time the unit attacks, which buys time against aggressive decks.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Saboteur (When this unit attacks, ignore Sentinel and defeat the defender's Shields.)
keyword.strategicValue: Gets past Sentinel and removes Shields, so it answers defensive boards.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Sentinel (Units in this arena can't attack your non-Sentinel units or your base.)
keyword.strategicValue: Forces opponents to attack this unit first, protecting your base and weaker units.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Shielded (When you play this unit, give him a Shield token.)
keyword.strategicValue: Gives the unit a Shield token on entry, absorbing the first damage it would take.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Smuggle [7 resources, vigilance] (If this card is a resource, you may play it for its smuggle cost. Replace it with the top card of your deck.)
keyword.strategicValue: Lets a card in your resource zone be played from there for a set cost, converting resources back into cards.

keyword.definition: Reminder text on the cards: Support (When you play this unit, you may attack with another unit. It gains this unit's other abilities for this attack.)
keyword.strategicValue: Lets a unit lend its abilities to another unit that attacks, so any unit can become a threat.

type.definition: Your base: one per deck, it starts in the base zone and has HP and an aspect icon. You lose when its damage reaches its HP.
type.strategicValue: Sets your aspect pool and your clock: more HP gives you more turns.

type.definition: A token introduced in A Lawless Time: while paying resources you may defeat it to pay 1 resource less.
type.strategicValue: Stored resource discount; it smooths expensive turns.

type.definition: A one-time effect. To play it you pay its cost, put it in your discard pile and resolve its ability, so it never enters play. It is normally played from your hand, but a card can allow another zone: Smuggle plays it from your resource zone and Plot plays it from your resource zone when you deploy a leader.
type.strategicValue: Flexible removal and tricks; cheap events can be played in any turn without leaving a target behind.

type.definition: A token for the Force: when you use the Force, remove it from play. Force tokens are created in the base zone.
type.strategicValue: Powers cards that ask you to use the Force.
type.source: rules digest section 4.2 and 8.38; card text

type.definition: Your leader: a double-sided card, one per deck (two in Twin Suns), that provides aspect icons and can deploy as a unit.
type.strategicValue: Defines the deck: its aspects and abilities decide which cards are cheap to play.

type.definition: The deployed side of a Leader card; the API records it as a second type (type2) on 512 printings across all sets.
type.strategicValue: What the leader becomes after you meet its deploy condition; its stats and abilities decide whether deploying is worth it.

type.definition: A unit created by an ability instead of coming from a deck. It is set aside when defeated.
type.strategicValue: Free board presence; the stronger tokens (such as Beast) cost more to create.

type.definition: An upgrade created by an ability, such as Shield, Experience, Advantage or Weakness. It is set aside when defeated.
type.strategicValue: Cheap stat or protection effects that cards hand out as rewards.

type.definition: A character or vehicle with power and HP. It enters play exhausted, stays in play until it is defeated, and fights in the ground or space arena by attacking enemy units or the enemy base.
type.strategicValue: The core of most decks; its cost, power and HP decide trades.

type.definition: A card that attaches to a unit, changes its stats and can grant abilities; it is defeated when the unit leaves play and can be played on enemy units.
type.strategicValue: Concentrates value on one unit, at the risk of losing both to one removal.

arena.definition: The ground arena is a zone shared by both players, next to each player's base zone. Ground units are played into it and can attack enemy ground units there or the enemy base without leaving it. The first unit played in the game decides which side of the base zone (left or right) the ground arena sits on, and the space arena takes the other side. Across all sets and printings, 5731 printings of 1319 distinct cards (counted by title and subtitle) are Ground. Among the 1609 in-scope cards, 856 are Ground.
arena.strategicValue: Most units and leaders are Ground, so Ground combat decides most games; Sentinel there blocks ground attackers only.

arena.definition: The shared zone where space units fight, on the opposite side from the ground arena. Across all sets and printings, 1841 printings of 420 distinct cards (counted by title and subtitle) are Space. Among the 1609 in-scope cards, 303 are Space.
arena.strategicValue: Space units can attack past ground defenders and are the usual hosts for Pilot cards; Homeworlds adds the first space leader unit.

rarity.definition: The most plentiful tier (letter C). Common cards fill most of every pack. Printed on the credit line (rules digest section 2).
rarity.strategicValue: Cheap to collect and usually low in price; the backbone of limited decks.

rarity.definition: The top pack tier (letter L), the scarcest pack rarity. Printed on the credit line (rules digest section 2).
rarity.strategicValue: Highest-impact cards and the highest prices among pack rarities.

rarity.definition: The third tier (letter R), scarcer than Uncommon. Printed on the credit line (rules digest section 2).
rarity.strategicValue: Strong effects and higher price than Uncommon.

rarity.definition: A tier (letter S) used for the extra cards in Spotlight Decks, for Intro Battle cards, for 66 Leader printings across all sets and for some promo printings; most Special cards are units. Printed on the credit line (rules digest section 2).
rarity.strategicValue: Often tied to a product, so supply follows the product rather than pack pull rates.

rarity.definition: The second tier (letter U), scarcer than Common. Printed on the credit line (rules digest section 2).
